profile.org_note: Founder-owned and founder-run from one corporate office in Sugar Land; the company publishes no leadership page. Texas Comptroller records show Jason Golan as president and director of Westin Homes Corporation (general partner of Westin Homes of Texas, Ltd.), manager of Westin Homes Houston, LLC and president of Westin Homes Austin, LLC, and registered agent of all seven Westin entities, so land and financing decisions run through him. A newer holding layer (Westin Homes Group, Ltd. and Westin Homes Holdings GP, LLC) was registered in June 2023. No CFO or division president is named by the company; the two land names below come only from contact directories.
profile.summary: Conventional private for-sale homebuilder, founder-owned by Jason Golan (first home 1994), building move-up and luxury homes on 40- to 80-foot lots inside third-party master-planned communities: 29 in Houston and 12 in Austin on the live site. The Builder 100 figures in the spine (rank 60, 1,062 closings, about $621M revenue for 2025) were seen only in search snippets of Builder's firm page, which blocks direct access. The company site lists Houston and Austin only: no San Antonio or Dallas-Fort Worth communities are shown, so the lead on those two markets is not confirmed. Westin buys finished lots from developers such as Johnson Development and Hines rather than developing its own land, which makes it a possible but not obvious land-banking customer.

people.name: Jason Golan
people.title: Founder and owner; President and Director, Westin Homes Corporation
people.source_title: Texas Comptroller franchise tax account status: Westin Homes Corporation (officers from Secretary of State, report year 2024)
people.note: State record lists him as President and Director of Westin Homes Corporation and registered agent of every Westin entity; the 2026 reports list him as Manager and Director of Westin Homes Houston, LLC and President and Director of Westin Homes Austin, LLC. Trade listings call him CEO; the BBB profile calls him Owner; a 2022 vendor case study and a 2014 company release call him founder and owner. The company site says the founder still reviews every plan. Phone is the published corporate main line.

gaps: CFO, controller and treasurer: not publicly disclosed. Contact directories showed two different names in search snippets (Phillip Fruge and Justin Hood as CFO, Priscilla Flanagan as controller); none could be confirmed on any openable page, the two CFO names conflict, and a follow-up search found nothing, so they are left out of the people list.

Head of land: not confirmed. The only names (Diane Danilov, VP of Land and Business Development; Matthew Voss, Director of Land Acquisition, Austin) come from contact directories and are tagged Inferred. No Houston land acquisition or land development head is named anywhere public.

Division presidents (Houston, Austin): not publicly disclosed. The BBB profile still lists Kyle Davison as Division President, but search snippets of a Builder Dealmakers speaker bio say he moved to Meritage Homes (Houston division president, then Texas region president from January 2025), so he is not listed as current. Directory snippets naming a division president (Lisa McCleskey) and an area president (Shannon Nelson) came from ZoomInfo, which mixes sales-award titles with officer titles, and were not confirmed.
President or COO separate from the founder: none found; state records show Jason Golan as president.

Other directors seen only as initials in a directory (Director of Construction C. M.; Director, Human Resources J. A.): names not public. The BBB profile also lists John Dewlen as Manager and customer contact; role and currency not confirmed.
Reporting lines: not published. In a founder-run company with no named president or COO the land and finance staff most likely report to Jason Golan, but no source states it.
San Antonio and Dallas-Fort Worth operations: not confirmed. The live company site lists only Houston and Austin; one directory mentions a 2022 Plano office, with no DFW communities found.
Builder 100 firm page (builderonline.com) blocks automated access, so rank, closings, revenue and the CEO listing were seen in search snippets only.
The shared web-search allowance ran out near the end of this run, so a last confirmation pass on the directory names was not possible.
